items.approval_reason: Addresses the massive neutral regime loss (-67.29R) with robust, multi-window validation (W1, W2, W3) and high trade retention (74.3%).
items.falsification_test: Run historical simulation of S01 excluding the neutral regime. If the net R improvement is less than 30R across W1, W2, and W3, or if trade retention falls below 70%, the hypothesis is falsified.
items.single_axis_change: Filter out entries during neutral regimes.

items.approval_reason: Neutral regime is the single largest source of loss (-188.34R) with an extremely low win rate (10.81%). Disabling it preserves the highly profitable long regime (+43.78R).
items.falsification_test: Backtest S02 by completely disabling entries when the regime is classified as 'neutral'. The hypothesis is falsified if the net R improvement is offset by a proportional loss of profitable trades in the long/short regimes, or if the profit factor does not rise above 1.0.

items.approval_reason: Extreme regime dependency. Long and short regimes generate massive net losses (-217.98R combined) with near-zero profit factors, while the neutral regime is highly profitable (+64.92R).
items.falsification_test: Run a historical simulation of S03 restricting entries strictly to the neutral regime. Falsified if the net R improvement does not exceed 150R or if trade retention drops below 40% of the total sample.
items.single_axis_change: Restrict strategy execution to neutral regimes only, disabling entries during long and short regimes.

items.approval_reason: Short regime filter shows consistent net R improvement across all three validation windows (W1: +12.01R, W2: +11.54R, W3: +1.60R).
items.falsification_test: Filter out short regime trades and measure performance across W1, W2, and W3. Falsified if net R delta becomes negative in W2 or W3.
items.single_axis_change: Exclude trade execution during short regime conditions.
